## Vercel + Vite SPA Deployment Config Research

### 1. SPA Rewrites
Vercel does NOT auto-configure SPA rewrites for Vite. You MUST add a vercel.json with:
{"rewrites": [{"source": "/(.*)", "destination": "/index.html"}]}
This is documented at vercel.com/docs/frameworks/frontend/vite under "Using Vite to make SPAs".

### 2. Framework Detection
Vercel auto-detects Vite via vite.config.ts and @vitejs/plugin-react. The framework slug is "vite". Defaults: buildCommand="vite build", outputDirectory="dist". However, SPA deep-linking does NOT work out of the box — requires manual vercel.json rewrites.

### 3. Build Output
Vercel auto-detects from vite.config.ts: buildCommand defaults to "vite build" (or package.json build script), outputDirectory defaults to "dist". No need to specify these unless overriding.

### 4. Install Command Override
Syntax: {"installCommand": "npm install --legacy-peer-deps"} in vercel.json. Supports any shell command string. Alternative: create .npmrc with legacy-peer-deps=true.

### 5. Complete vercel.json for this project:
{
  "$schema": "https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json",
  "framework": "vite",
  "installCommand": "npm install --legacy-peer-deps",
  "rewrites": [{"source": "/(.*)", "destination": "/index.html"}]
}

### Key Notes
- react/react-dom are peerDependencies in this project — Vercel npm install may fail without --legacy-peer-deps or --install-peers
- createBrowserRouter from react-router v7 requires SPA rewrites or all deep links will 404
- No need to specify buildCommand or outputDirectory — Vite preset handles it
- The framework slug "vite" is correct; "react-router" slug exists but is for React Router framework mode (SSR), not SPA mode

RESEARCH FINDINGS - Peer Dependency & Package Manager Evaluation for Vercel Deploy.

=== 1. npm 7+ peerDependencies behavior ===
- npm 7+ AUTO-INSTALLS regular peer deps by default.
- HOWEVER, peerDependenciesMeta.optional:true causes npm to SKIP auto-install of those peers.
- THIS IS THE ROOT CAUSE: react and react-dom are in peerDependencies with optional:true, so npm SKIPS them.
- Locally it works because package-lock.json (lockfileVersion:3) already has react resolved as peer:true from a prior install.
- On Vercel fresh install with no cached node_modules, npm will NOT install optional peers.

=== 2. .npmrc approach ===
- legacy-peer-deps=true: Makes npm behave like npm v6 (ignores peer deps entirely). Does NOT help — it PREVENTS peer dep installation, making things worse.
- auto-install-peers is a PNPM setting, NOT an npm setting. It does nothing in .npmrc for npm.
- For npm: There is NO .npmrc setting that forces installation of optional peer deps.
- BEST FIX FOR NPM: Move react/react-dom from peerDependencies to dependencies. This is the correct fix.
- Vercel DOES respect .npmrc files during builds.

=== 3. pnpm approach ===
- pnpm 8/9/10 has auto-install-peers=true BY DEFAULT.
- pnpm auto-installs non-optional peer deps. For optional peers, behavior is inconsistent (known bug pnpm#8142).
- Project already has pnpm.overrides section — partially pnpm-ready.
- MIXING npm locally + pnpm on Vercel is NOT recommended. Lock files conflict. ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE errors.
- If switching to pnpm: must use pnpm everywhere (local + CI + Vercel). Must generate pnpm-lock.yaml, remove package-lock.json.
- Figma Make generates package.json for npm — switching to pnpm adds friction for their workflow.

=== 4. Vercel defaults (2025/2026) ===
- Default Node.js: 24.x (ships with npm 11).
- npm 11 inherits same behavior: optional peer deps are NOT auto-installed.
- Vercel detects package manager from lock file: package-lock.json -> npm, pnpm-lock.yaml -> pnpm.
- No lock file -> Vercel defaults to npm.
- Current project has package-lock.json (lockfileVersion:3) -> Vercel uses npm 10 (Node 22 mapping) or npm 11 (Node 24).
- Vercel respects .npmrc files and installCommand overrides.

=== RECOMMENDED SOLUTION ===
The simplest and most correct fix: Move react and react-dom from peerDependencies to dependencies.
This ensures both npm and pnpm install them. Works on Vercel with zero config changes.
The peerDependencies + optional:true pattern is designed for LIBRARIES (where the consumer provides react).
This is an APPLICATION (private:true), so react belongs in dependencies.

ALTERNATIVE: Keep current structure but add installCommand override in vercel.json: npm install --install-strategy=nested, or override install to explicitly add react.

LOCAL STATE: Node 22.21.1, npm 10.9.4, package-lock.json lockfileVersion:3, react IS installed locally (resolved as peer:true in lockfile from prior install).

FIGMA MAKE COMPATIBILITY RESEARCH (2026-03-01). FINDING 1 - FILES MANAGED BY FIGMA MAKE: Figma Make pushes via figma[bot] with commit message "Add files from Figma Make". It overwrites the ENTIRE repo contents on each push. Files managed: package.json, vite.config.ts, postcss.config.mjs, index.html, README.md, ATTRIBUTIONS.md, guidelines/Guidelines.md, src/main.tsx, src/app/**/*.tsx, src/styles/**/*.css, src/imports/**. The GitHub push is ONE-WAY (Figma->GitHub) and assumes files have not been moved/restructured. Manual changes in GitHub WILL BE OVERWRITTEN on next push. FINDING 2 - SAFE FILES: .npmrc (safe - Figma docs mention it for private registry), vercel.json (safe - not part of Figma Make output), .gitignore (CAUTION - Figma Make creates one with just "node_modules", may be overwritten), tsconfig.json (safe - Figma Make does not generate one), .env/.env.local (safe - never generated). Custom root config files are safe IF not in Figma Make managed set. RECOMMENDED: use a separate branch for deployment config or add files Figma Make does not know about. FINDING 3 - WHY peerDependencies: Figma Make preview runs in browser with esm.sh CDN providing React. React is a peerDependency+optional because: (a) Make preview provides React via esm.sh at runtime, (b) marking optional prevents npm install errors when React is externally provided, (c) allows the package to work in both Make preview and local dev. For local dev, React gets installed automatically by npm7+ anyway. FINDING 4 - ADDING FILES SAFELY: Figma Make overwrites entire repo on push. Strategy: (a) work on a separate branch (e.g., deploy or dev), (b) merge Figma Make changes from main into your branch, (c) keep custom config files (.npmrc, vercel.json, tsconfig.json) on your branch, (d) files in directories Figma Make does not use (e.g., /config, /scripts, /public) are less likely to conflict but still at risk of deletion on force-push. KEY RISK: Figma Make push may DELETE files it does not know about since it replaces repo contents entirely.

RESEARCH: 7 options for deploying Vite+React18 to Vercel with react/react-dom in peerDependencies (optional via peerDependenciesMeta). CRITICAL FINDING: react/react-dom ARE already in package-lock.json because sub-deps (MUI, Radix, cmdk, lucide-react, etc) have react as non-optional peer dep. npm install on Vercel will install them from lockfile. RANKED OPTIONS: (1) BEST: vercel.json installCommand="npm install" + commit package-lock.json - simplest, react already in lockfile, no local breakage. (2) GOOD: postinstall script "postinstall":"npm install react@18.3.1 react-dom@18.3.1 --no-save" - explicit guarantee, works everywhere, no package.json changes. (3) GOOD: Switch to pnpm - auto-install-peers=true default in v8+, project already has pnpm.overrides, need to generate pnpm-lock.yaml and delete package-lock.json. (4) OK: vercel.json installCommand="npm install && npm install react@18.3.1 react-dom@18.3.1 --no-save" - belt-and-suspenders, only affects Vercel. (5) AVOID: .npmrc auto-install-peers=true - this is pnpm-only setting, NOT npm. For npm it does nothing. Even for pnpm, does NOT install optional peers (peerDependenciesMeta optional:true). (6) AVOID: .npmrc legacy-peer-deps=true - wrong tool, this PREVENTS peer dep installation not enables it. (7) N/A: NPM_FLAGS env var - Vercel does not support NPM_FLAGS, use NPM_RC env var instead with .npmrc contents. (8) N/A: framework:vite in vercel.json - does not affect dependency installation at all. CONCLUSION: Option 1 (just deploy with package-lock.json committed) should work as-is. Option 2 (postinstall) is the safest belt-and-suspenders. Option 3 (pnpm) is cleanest long-term.

Status flow: Subida->Verificada or Rechazada. 7) Team roles: Owner(full), Editor(edit modules/upload), Viewer(read-only). 8) Step 1 Module C semaphore: verde(advance)/amarillo(review)/rojo(blocked) based on constraints completeness. 9) Step 2: min 10 ideas, 3 clusters, max 5 finalists, DVF scoring 1-5. 10) Step 3: Go/Iterar/No-Go/Pivote decision. 11) Step 4: Narrativa + Evidence selection + Deck generation. 12) Mentor rubric: 5 criteria x 5 points (evidencia, consistencia, claridad, accionabilidad, riesgos). ## 3. PLATFORM vs PROJECT SCOPE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

### Platform-level roles (User.role — stored in User table, in JWT):
| Role | Scope | Rationale |
|------|-------|-----------|
| participante | Platform | Can create projects, has own dashboard, self-registers |
| mentor | Platform | Assigned to projects by admin, has mentor panel |
| admin | Platform | Full platform access, manages everything |
| sponsor | Platform | Strategic role, assigned to projects, has own dashboard view |

### Project-level roles (TeamMember.role — stored in TeamMember table):
| Role | Scope | Rationale |
|------|-------|-----------|
| OWNER | Project | Project creator, maps to participante who created it |
| COLLABORATOR | Project | Team member invited by participant, permission-based |
| VIEWER | Project | Read-only access at project level |
| SPONSOR | Project | Sponsor assigned to this specific project |

### CRITICAL DESIGN DECISION:
- Sponsor is BOTH platform-level AND project-level (User.role=sponsor + TeamMember.role=SPONSOR)
- Colaborador is PROJECT-LEVEL ONLY (no platform-level role — they are participantes or external users who have a collaborator relationship to specific projects)
- Viewer/Invitado: PROJECT-LEVEL for project-specific access; could also be platform-level for "guest" users who have no own projects
- Recommendation: Keep 4 platform roles (participante, mentor, admin, sponsor) + evolve TeamRole enum to (OWNER, COLLABORATOR, VIEWER, SPONSOR)
